sites.name: Apollo 17
sites.description: A valley enclosed by steep massifs. Surface images show gray soil, scattered fragments, tracks and sharply defined shadows.
sites.dem: 2 m LROC NAC in the current preset
sites.renderNote: This saved example preserves the earlier appearance-study geometry. Rebuild with the current extension for its native 2 m crop. Camera pose and small features are illustrative.
sites.photoCaption: AS17-147-22527: lunar module and rover on the Apollo 17 surface.

sites.name: Chang’e-6
sites.description: A mare surface inside the Apollo basin. The panorama provides a reference for fine regolith and scattered fragments.
sites.dem: 4 m LROC NAC in the current preset
sites.renderNote: The saved example preserves earlier geometry. Rebuild for the native 4 m crop. The panorama and render do not share a camera pose.
sites.photoCaption: Stitched panorama from the Chang’e-6 lander, released 4 June 2024.

sites.name: Blue Ghost 1
sites.description: Low-Sun mare terrain near Mons Latreille. The appearance preset uses cool color balance, long shadows and sparse fragments.
sites.renderNote: Native 3 m terrain is included. The cool tint is a photographic interpretation, not a measured blue soil spectrum. No lander or Earth model is included.
sites.photoCaption: Blue Ghost’s shadow on Mare Crisium after landing on 2 March 2025.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3
sites.role: Coordinates printed on ISRO’s annotated surface image
sites.description: Pragyan’s grayscale NavCam images show fine soil, scattered small rocks and a low horizon. The example uses rover-height framing.
sites.renderNote: Native pre-landing 3 m DEM. Vikram, tracks and plume-disturbed soil are not reconstructed. At 69° S, this location lies outside the polar inset.
sites.photoCaption: Pragyan view of Vikram from about 15 m, 30 August 2023, 11:04 IST.

sites.name: Moon Base target region
sites.status: Blue Moon Mark 1 target region · 2027 schedule
sites.role: NASA R01 regional reference; not a confirmed touchdown fix
sites.description: A ridge between deeply shadowed craters. NASA identifies this region for an early Moon Base mission; the permanent base location remains under study.
sites.renderNote: The saved 40 km scene includes surface and regional-overview cameras. Sun elevation is illustrative at 1.4°. The legacy SOUTH preset retains its earlier nearby origin.
sites.photoCaption: LROC oblique view of the Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge, M1348682369LR. Regional context, not a surface view at the preset origin.

sources.title: 2025 Lunar Surface Data Book, table A2.1-1, p. 75

sites.name: VIPER
sites.role: Published primary mission-area center; not a touchdown fix
sites.description: The mission area lies on the southern edge of Mons Mouton, near Nobile crater. Its varied illumination and thermal environments are relevant to water-ice prospecting.
sites.dem: 5 m adjusted LOLA at the origin
sites.context: 3 m NAC where valid / 80 m regional / 473.8 m wider context
sites.renderNote: The 3 m stereo footprint has a gap at this exact reference point, so valid 5 m LOLA supplies its height. The polar Hapke appearance is an Apollo analogue. No VIPER rover model is included.
sites.photoCaption: LROC low-Sun mosaic of the broader Mons Mouton Plateau. Black areas include shadows and mosaic gaps. No VIPER surface photographs exist yet.
sites.credit: NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University / Intuitive Machines

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.status: Candidate region in NASA’s October 2024 shortlist
sites.description: A polar rim region useful for exploring relief and grazing illumination away from Connecting Ridge. Its historical candidate status is not a final mission assignment.
sites.renderNote: Exploratory region preset, not a landing-safety assessment. Small craters and rocks are procedural, and the Sun is illustrative.
sites.photoCaption: LROC Nobile Rim 2 controlled mosaic B from low-Sun orbital images. Black regions include deep shadow and mosaic gaps.
sites.credit: NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University / Intuitive Machines

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.status: Candidate region in NASA’s October 2024 shortlist
sites.role: NASA R23 regional reference; distinct from IM-1
sites.description: A prominent highland massif with substantial relief. The oblique orbital image illustrates why broad elevation context matters for polar scenes.
sites.context: 5 m LOLA fallback / 80 m regional / 473.8 m wider context
sites.renderNote: This reference is separate from the IM-1 landing site. The ground-level render is a terrain study, not the orbital camera perspective.
sites.photoCaption: LROC oblique view of Malapert Massif, acquired 3 March 2023, NAC M1432398306LR.
